text:
The Federal Government has introduced a business support programme to empower 600 tailors across Nigeria, with each selected beneficiary expected to receive ₦5 million in grants and repayable business financing.
The initiative, known as the Business Incubation for Renewed Hope Tailors Programme, will run for five years and is being implemented through the Industrial Training Fund (ITF).
The programme is designed to help skilled artisans establish, strengthen and expand their tailoring businesses, while creating employment opportunities across the country.
The ITF announced the initiative during a pre-launch sensitisation exercise in Jos, Plateau State, where it disclosed that 150 tailors from the North-Central zone had been selected for the pilot phase.
The initiative is one of the exit pathways under the ITF’s Skill-Up Artisans Programme (SUPA), which seeks to improve the technical and business skills of Nigerian artisans.
The programme is open to both participants of the ITF’s Skill-Up Artisans Programme and tailors who received their training outside the scheme.
However, prospective beneficiaries must meet specific requirements to qualify.
The ITF has not announced a separate nationwide application deadline or confirmed that a fresh application window for all 600 beneficiaries is currently open.
However, its general Business Incubation Programme guidelines provide for registration through the Fund’s area offices.
Interested artisans can visit the nearest ITF area office to obtain and complete the business incubation application form.
They can also visit the Fund’s official website, www.itf.gov.ng, for information about its programmes and application procedures.
Tailors who did not participate in SUPA must ensure they obtain the required ITF certification and licence to meet the eligibility conditions.
The ITF’s general business incubation guidelines also state that participation in the incubation programme is free.
Applicants should note that registering for SUPA or submitting an application for the general business incubation programme does not automatically guarantee selection for the Renewed Hope Tailors initiative.
Although 150 beneficiaries have already been selected from the North-Central zone, the ITF has yet to provide a detailed selection timetable for the remaining 450 places.
The Director-General of ITF, Dr Afiz Oluwatoyin Ogun, represented by the Director of Legal Services, Safiya Abubakar, said the initiative aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda, which seeks to upgrade the skills of Nigerian artisans to international standards.
According to her, the programme would provide selected tailors with a structured opportunity to develop their businesses from start-up level to maturity over five years.
She urged prospective beneficiaries to pay attention to the programme’s processes and requirements.
